home_title: AI is coming home. Decide what it may do.
home_lead: The Home-Mandate Specification is an open standard that lets every household say what an AI agent may do – allow, ask or deny.
home_meta: Open specification · Text CC BY 4.0 · Code Apache 2.0
home_card_foot: Decided inside your home – not by the agent.
home_decisions_lead: Every request from an agent gets exactly one answer. You can read it like a house rule.
home_allow_body: The request runs right away. No one is disturbed.
home_ask_body: A person confirms on their phone. Without an answer, nothing happens.
home_deny_body: The request is refused – no matter who asks or how.
home_rule_body: anything not explicitly allowed is not allowed.
home_scenario_lead: The same mandate answers each one. The decision is made in your home.
home_step1_title: The voice assistant turns on the light
home_step1_body: Lights are allowed in the mandate. It happens at once.
home_step1_alt: The agent asks the home, the home answers allow: the light goes on.
home_step2_title: An agent wants to open the front door
home_step2_body: Doors need a person. Alex gets a question on the phone and approves.
home_step2_alt: The agent asks the home, the home answers ask: a phone shows the question “Open the front door?” with Approve and Decline.
home_step3_title: A forged e-mail tries to switch off the alarm
home_step3_body: The agent was tricked – but the mandate says no. The alarm stays on.
home_step3_alt: A forged e-mail reaches the agent, the agent asks the home, the home answers deny: the alarm stays on.
home_start_title: Where would you like to start?
home_start_why_body: What a mandate does in everyday life – and why your smart home app alone is not enough.
home_start_play_body: Build a mandate by clicking and test requests right in your browser.
home_start_spec_body: Specification, JSON schemas and conformance tests.
home_open_body: The specification belongs to no product. Any vendor can implement it and check their conformance with public tests.
